paper_title: Real-world safety of aliskiren in primary hypertension: A cross-database study
study_design: Retrospective cross-database analysis of aliskiren-associated spontaneous reports. FAERS extraction is described through OpenVigil 2.1 with primary-suspect selection and latest-FDA_DT deduplication for the same CASEID. MedDRA 26.0 standardization precedes descriptive, disproportionality and time-to-onset analyses.
evidence_type: Descriptive spontaneous-report characteristics; ROR/PRR and Bayesian BCPNN/MGPS reporting-signal measures; report-based time-to-onset summaries.
claim: The study characterizes aliskiren-associated spontaneous reports in two complementary reporting systems.
context: Retrospective FAERS and WHO-VigiAccess pharmacovigilance, with database totals kept separate.
reported_evidence: [{"label":"FAERS reports","value":"5,596 aliskiren-associated reports"},{"label":"VigiAccess reports","value":"5,549 aliskiren-associated reports"},{"label":"Evidence unit","value":"Spontaneously submitted suspected-event reports, not the number of exposed patients"},{"label":"Methods","value":"ROR, PRR, BCPNN and MGPS disproportionality methods; MedDRA version 26.0 PT/SOC standardization"}]
source_locator: Method: Data sources (sec003), Data standardization (sec004), Statistical analysis (sec005). Results: Descriptive analysis of AE report characteristics (sec007); Tables 1-2.
scope_does_not_establish: ["Incidence, absolute or comparative patient risk, a causal adverse-drug reaction, or the relative safety of aliskiren versus another treatment.","A pooled independent cohort from the two database totals, or event-probability/hazard estimates from cumulative percentages of submitted reports.","New prescribing restrictions, screening recommendations or proof that an unlisted event is an established aliskiren adverse reaction."]
limitations: ["Spontaneous reports are subject to missingness, reporting differences, confounding and possible overlap between databases; there is no exposed-patient denominator for incidence or causal risk.","The main FAERS window is internally inconsistent: Methods 2004 Q1-2025 Q3, Table 1 caption Q4 2023-Q4 2024 and annual entries 2005-2025 in S3.","Table 1 reports 1,037 Serious records but 1,735 Hospitalization entries and 3,080 Other Serious Medical Events; the report-versus-outcome relationship is not sufficiently explained to reconcile these counts.","S4 preferred-term comparison cells use a 17,094 target-drug term-count total rather than the 5,549 descriptive reports, and some stored estimates differ from printed main-table values; exact quantitative signal ranking requires clarification.","Onset dates are missing or invalid for 3,387 FAERS reports (60.53%). Unequal or open-ended time bins and a cumulative report-time curve do not establish a bimodal patient hazard."]
single_finding_matrix_scope: ["Retrospective FAERS and WHO-VigiAccess pharmacovigilance, with database totals kept separate."]
export_notice: Study-level author-maintained evidence summary. Not participant-level data and not a ready-to-pool meta-analysis dataset. For formal citation, use the original article DOI.
